verdict.rationale: Founder Law publishes its own explainer pages on startup visa pathways. The International Entrepreneur Parole page includes concrete, CPI-adjusted qualifying thresholds, the employment-based visas page explains EB-1A self-petitioning, and a Techstars immigration library offers resources to read 'at your own pace'. However, that library is framed as packaged for Techstars members, the deeper Extraordinary Ability Bootcamp is a paid course, and nothing shows real case examples or confirms the guides are ungated. Missing for 10: evidence of real worked examples or case studies, confirmation that the guides are openly accessible rather than member- or lead-gated, depth of process explainers beyond single-page summaries, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, the provider publishes substantial free guides on startup visas — criteria breakdowns, process explainers, real examples — open to anyone, not gated lead bait

citations.quote: Your startup has received at least $264,147* from qualified U.S. investors or at least $105,659* in government awards or grants
startup founders can obtain up to a 30-month immigration status called “Parole” to live in the U.S. with their families and scale their startup.
